idea-plugin.name: Next Key
idea-plugin.description:
Hold a modifier key and see what you can press next.

Hold Ctrl for half a second and a panel lists every shortcut that starts with Ctrl. Keep holding and add Alt — the list becomes the Ctrl+Alt shortcuts. Let go and it disappears. Shortcuts that take two presses work the same way: press the first, and every key that can follow appears.

The list is read from your own keymap, so it matches the bindings you actually have, including the ones other plugins add. Entries are grouped by what they do, and keys are labelled the way they are on your keyboard.

The panel starts out listing the shortcuts most people use. In Settings | Tools | Next Key you can show or hide any shortcut, rename one, move it to another category, change how long a modifier has to be held, and adjust transparency.

Available in English and Simplified Chinese. Source and issue tracker on GitHub.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.0

  • The hold delay is configurable, from 100 to 2000 ms
  • Adjustable popup opacity
  • Key names now match the keyboard: [, /, PgUp, ↑ instead of the internal names Swing reports. They no longer follow the OS locale either
  • Keys are drawn as keycaps; the popup has rounded corners
  • Long action names are truncated so one entry cannot widen a whole column
  • The interface language now follows the IDE language setting rather than the operating system locale
  • The shortcut index is built in the background at startup, so the very first press shows the popup right away
  • Enabling the plugin from Settings | Plugins now takes effect immediately, without restarting the IDE

0.3.0

  • Entries are grouped by category
  • Settings UI for showing, renaming and re-categorizing individual shortcuts
  • English and Simplified Chinese interface
  • Listeners are now removed when the plugin is disabled or unloaded
